body: Needless whitespace change, it's just diff pollution.
Should be moved outside of the for-loop since the result is cascade-independant. There's no point in recomputing it every time.
I might be biased since I wrote this comment, but why was it removed?
Very minor aesthetic nitpick, but this probably fits better alongside the `light_frustum_planes.write[5]` block, since that part of the code is also culling-related.
Is there a reason for changing this comment? To me it seems unrelated to the PR's changes. If there's no reason for the change, then it's just diff noise.
There's no need to change this, it just pollutes the diff.
Since this isn't storing only cull planes anymore, maybe it could be renamed to something like `DirectionalLightCullData`?
As `RenderingLightCuller::prepare_directional_light` no longer calls `_prepare_light`, this is dead code and can be removed.

As the `Vector<Plane> receiver_frustum_planes = camera_matrix.get_projection_planes(p_cam_transform)` line should already be moved away from here, the changes to the comment formatting aren't needed and just make the diff more noisy. The rendering codebase already has a lot of incorrectly-formatted 5+ years-old comments anyway.

As I understand it, `prepare_directional_light` and `prepare_directional_light_cascade` need to be called both and in order for everything to work properly. So maybe they could be renamed to `prepare_directional_light_begin_preparing` and `prepare_directional_light_prepare_cascade` to highlight that?

...Maybe those names aren't the best, I just thought of how `draw_list_begin` in the rendering device works since it feels kind of similar.

Unless I'm misunderstanding the suggestion, I think this needs to remain inside the loop. camera_matrix is rebuilt for each cascade using that cascade's near/far distances, so get_projection_planes() returns cascade-specific planes. Moving it outside would only calculate one cascade's receiver frustum.
I think I removed it accidentally while cleaning up the old cascade setup and overlooked it
Yes, I will revert it
Yeah thats fine

I get what you mean, but this uses receiver_frustum_planes and endpoints, not light_frustum_planes, it makes more sense right after get_endpoints() since that’s where both inputs are ready, what do u think?
No real reason, just shortened it while cleaning the code, I'll restore it
Yeah since it now stores the light source too it makes sense

Yeah both calls are needed in order. prepare_directional_light_begin_preparing() feels a bit long though, how about begin_directional_light() and keeping prepare_directional_light_cascade() for the second one?
Yeah no, I messed up here. Somehow I only looked at `p_cam_transform` and didn't notice `camera_matrix` being created per-cascade.

`prepare_directional_light_begin` and `prepare_directional_light_cascade` are probably the best we're going to get, if we're trying to keep them short. Mostly for consistency with the similar `prepare_regular_light`.
That's also fine.
